deep.reconstruction:
This folio is a heavily revised draft of the opening of Part II of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). Several crossed-out first lines and a crossed-out title ('Theorie der algebraischen Functionen', corrected to 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen') show him trying out the opening sentence. The text that survives does the following.

(1) Setup. Let s be an algebraic function of z. Then s and z satisfy an equation F(s,z)=0 with F a polynomial; F is irreducible, of degree n in s and degree m in z. Equivalently,
  a_0(z) s^n + a_1(z) s^(n-1) + ... + a_n(z) = 0, with deg a_i <= m.
Hence to each value of z there correspond n values of s.

(2) The Riemann surface. The branching of this function is represented by a surface T spread over the z-plane. T covers every part of the plane n times. On T, s becomes a single-valued function of position.

(3) Poles of s. This function becomes infinite of the first order at m points of T and is continuous elsewhere. The justification is mine, not on the page: for a fixed value c, F(c,z)=0 has m roots z, so s takes every value m times on the closed surface. In particular s has m poles counted with multiplicity.

(4) Closing the surface. An unbounded surface can be regarded either as having an infinitely distant boundary or as a closed surface. Riemann adopts the second view: in each of the n sheets the point z=infinity closes the surface off in a point, unless a branching occurs at z=infinity. (A parenthesis is left blank in the manuscript.)

(5) Rational functions. Every rational function of s and z is also a single-valued function of position on T, not discontinuous along any line. It therefore has the same branching ('Verzweigungsart') as s. In modern terms, C(z,s) is the function field of the compact surface T.

(6) Integrals. The page breaks off here. By integrating such a function one obtains a function that is single-valued after T is cut into a simply connected surface T*. The next page continues: the cut system has 2p cross-cuts, and the jumps across each cut are constant.

No computations appear on the page. It is purely the conceptual set-up of the published memoir.
errors: 'Infinite of the first order at m points' holds only generically. In general s has m poles counted with multiplicity (equal to the number of z-roots of F(c,z)=0). They are simple and finite only when, for example, a_0(z) has m distinct roots and deg a_0 = m, so that s stays finite over z=infinity. The published version carries the same implicit genericity assumption.
The sentence about closing the surface at z=infinity is unfinished (an empty parenthesis is left in the manuscript). It is not an error, just incomplete draft wording.

results.what: Algebraic function s(z) defined by an irreducible F(s,z)=0 of bidegree (n,m), represented as a single-valued function on an n-sheeted surface T over the z-plane
results.modern_name: Riemann surface of an algebraic function / compact Riemann surface of the plane curve F=0

results.what: s takes each value m times on T, so it has m poles (generically simple)
results.modern_name: degree of the meromorphic function s : T -> P^1 equals deg_z F

results.what: Compactifying T by adding the points over z=infinity
Rational functions of s and z are single-valued on T with the same branching
results.modern_name: function field C(z,s) = field of meromorphic functions on T
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 (equivalence classes of curves under birational transformation)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a preparatory draft of the well-known opening of Part II of Riemann's published 1857 memoir. Its only interest is the visible process of revision, for example the title change and the choice to treat the surface as closed.

checkable.asserts: For F of degree m=2 in z, a fixed value s=c is attained at m=2 values of z. Hence s has m poles on T, counted with multiplicity.
The degree in s equals n=2, so each z has n=2 values of s, giving a 2-sheeted surface T.
Example with n=2, m=1: s=+-1/sqrt(z). Its single pole lies over the branch point z=0 and is simple in the local parameter t=sqrt(z), consistent with m=1 pole.

transcription_corrections: Line 1 should read roughly '[-Abel'sche-] Theorie der {+Abel'schen+} [-algebraischen-] Functionen'. The struck heading is a title draft.
'welche für m Punkte derselben unendlich von der ersten Ordnung wird, übrigens aber stetig ist' is read correctly.
The phrase rendered 'diese Fläche in Punkte aufschließt' is probably 'diese Fläche in einem Punkte abschließt' (closes off the surface in a point at z=infinity).

'Jede rationale Function von s und z ist offenbar ebenfalls eine eindeutig bestimmte und nicht längs einer Linie unstetige Function des Orts in der Fläche T' is read correctly. The insertion 'und besitzt also dieselbe Verzweigungsart wie die Function s' belongs to it.
The last lines probably read 'Durch Integration einer solchen Function erhält man ... wenn man die Fläche T in eine einfach zusammenhängende T* zerschneidet'.
